why:
The Slav is your answer to 1.d4. You play 1...d5. After 2.c4 you play 2...c6. The c6 pawn guards d5, so your centre pawn has support. The Caro-Kann uses the same idea.

In most lines your light-squared bishop comes out to f5 or g4 before you play ...e6. Then ...e6 does not shut the bishop in. There are exceptions. If White plays Nc3 and e3 before Nf3, you play ...e6 early. Then the bishop stays at home for a while. Later ...dxc4 and ...b5 give it the b7 square.

The opening asks for patience. Develop your pieces, castle short, and then use a pawn break. Your breaks are ...c5 and ...e5.

Against 2.Bf4 you do not play ...c6. You play ...c5 and attack the d4 pawn. Against 1.c4 and 1.Nf3 you often reach the Slav by a different move order.

variations.middlegame:
After ...Bb4 you play ...Nbd7 and castle short. A typical order is O-O Nbd7 Qe2 Bg6 e4 O-O. Move the bishop to g6 before White plays e4. The e4 pawn would attack the bishop on f5.

Your pawn breaks are ...e5 and ...c5. Both hit the d4 pawn. Play ...e5 only when your pieces guard it. After Bd3 Re8 Rd1, the d7 knight and the e8 rook guard e5.

In the ...e6 set-up (Nc3 and e3 before Nf3), your c8 bishop comes out to b7 after ...dxc4 and ...b5. Then ...c5 opens its diagonal.

mistakes.text: Do not play ...b5 here to keep the pawn. After axb5 cxb5 Nxb5, White has the pawn back, the half-open a-file and the better game. Play ...Bf5 and give the pawn back later.
Do not play ...e6 before ...Bf5. Your c8 bishop would have only the d7 square. It is not a blunder, but it breaks your plan. Play ...Bf5 first.
Do not play ...e5 yet. The d4 pawn and the f3 knight attack e5, and only the d7 knight guards it. White wins material, for example with Nxe5. Play ...Re8 first. Then the rook guards e5 too.

If White plays Bd3, trade bishops. Then pin the c3 knight with ...Bb4, and castle short. A typical order is Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 Bb4 O-O O-O.

Both sides have an open c-file. Your pawn on d5 is attacked by the c3 knight, so keep it guarded. If a white rook comes to c1, trade ...Bxc3 and play ...Ne4. The d5 pawn guards that knight.
